name: FL-19
label: Likely R

key_factors: Republican nominee has raised over $2 million vs. minimal Democratic fundraising
Open seat after Byron Donalds retired to run for governor
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
model.rationale: The district's R+14 lean, the Republican nominee's large fundraising advantage, and markets pricing a Republican win near 94% all point to a safe Republican hold despite the open seat. No polls or expert ratings provide any reason to move materially away from that picture.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending or a competitive multi-candidate Republican primary hangover could narrow the margin somewhat, but a Democratic win would require an extraordinary shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Byron Donalds (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Byron Donalds is leaving this southwest Florida seat to run for governor, creating an open contest in a district that leans heavily Republican. The Republican nominee, Jim Schwartzel, has raised more than $2 million, while Democrat Victor Arias has raised under $50,000 and has little cash on hand. An independent candidate is also on the ballot with negligible funding.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's strong Republican baseline and the lopsided money gap. Prediction markets give the Democrat only a small chance of winning. The seat is expected to remain in Republican hands by a wide margin, with modest uncertainty from the open-seat dynamic.
